My projects

Leonardo da Vinci’s aerial screw, modelled in Blender and animated in Unity so it actually flies. You can try it out yourself on itch.io.

  • Modelled the wooden base, the cloth screw and all the rope rigging in Blender
  • Animated it in Unity so it spins up and takes off
  • Published a playable version on itch.io
Try it on itch.io

A project for the Dutch National Police, made with five teammates. The question was how neighbours can support each other during a long power outage. Our answer is a board by the front door where residents slip in a colored card: green means “I can help”, orange means “I need help” and red means “I need help now”.

  • Went from a paper prototype to a cardboard one to a finished board with a screen
  • Added an optional digital layer: light sensors and an ESP32 send each status to a hub with a tree that grows every time someone gets helped
  • Tested it with young adults in a simulated blackout

An interactive art installation about a hard decision, built as a hospital room for an exhibition at Black Brick. Visitors put on headphones, watch a short video, choose option A or B with a button and sign a form.

  • Built together as a team: a laser-cut heart rate monitor, nurse call handsets, an IV drip made from resealable bags, and a bed with a mannequin
  • Wired LED strips to the buttons and videos, and resoldered the cables when the lights failed at the last moment
  • Recorded the voice acting ourselves at the Design Lab of the University of Twente

A poster for a behavioural change assignment, aimed at doomscrolling. I wanted it to hit hard, so I went for a dark, high-contrast look with a bold headline and a bomb with a “scrolls left” countdown.

  • Wrote the headline: “Stop scrolling to your doom.”
  • Built the layout, typography and imagery
  • Styled it like an official government campaign

A traditional Japanese house modelled from scratch in Blender.

  • Modelled the curved, tiled roof and the L-shaped floor plan
  • Made the gridded sliding walls and the wooden entrance steps
  • Set up warm interior lighting so the house glows from within

A set of Blender animation exercises, from simple physics to character animation.

  • A ball rolling down a curved ramp into a cup
  • A rigged character that waves, animated by posing its armature frame by frame

For Module 2 I set myself a challenge: get better at photography. I ended up shooting modern buildings with sharp lines and clean textures, then editing them with more contrast and tight crops for an abstract, brutalist look. Use the switch to compare with the originals.

  • Learned how exposure and composition work, and how to edit to a consistent style
  • Planned three months but did most of it in one short burst, which I liked

A hands-on electronics build: a Christmas tree circuit board that lights up once it’s assembled.

  • Soldered every component onto the blue PCB trees by hand
  • Followed the build instructions and trimmed the leads with side cutters
  • Worked at a soldering station in the lab
